requirements.requirement: Provide an encrypted volume on node1 (LUKS2-backed) mounted at /srv/secure
requirements.summary: A 2GiB LUKS2 container was created via cryptsetup luksFormat (LUKS_FORMAT_OK), opened, formatted ext4, and mounted at /srv/secure showing 2.0G capacity and ext4 filesystem type via df -h/mount.

requirements.requirement: Volume unlocks automatically at boot (no manual passphrase/intervention)
requirements.summary: A crypttab entry referencing a root-only (0600) keyfile with 'luks,nofail' options was added; after a full reboot, systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service was observed active without any manual unlock step.

requirements.requirement: Volume mounts automatically at boot at /srv/secure and persists data across restart
requirements.summary: fstab entry configured with nofail; pre-reboot baseline captured boot_id a0c36ad2... and md5sum of a test file; reboot was issued and confirmed via unreachability then a new boot_id (3976e255...) with uptime 0; post-reboot check shows srv-secure.mount active, /srv/secure mounted, and the test file's content/md5sum identical to baseline, directly demonstrating a complete healthy-baseline -> disruption -> recovery transition.

requirements.requirement: systemd correctly generates unlock/mount units from crypttab/fstab config (pre-reboot sanity check)
requirements.summary: After manually unmounting and closing the LUKS device, the executor triggered systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service and srv-secure.mount (both shown as generated from /etc/crypttab and /etc/fstab) and confirmed both started successfully and remounted the volume with the test file intact, prior to the full reboot test.

overall_summary: The executor created a LUKS2-encrypted, file-backed volume on node1, configured crypttab/fstab with a root-only keyfile for hands-off unlock, validated the generated systemd units pre-reboot, and then directly demonstrated the full boot-time behavior via an actual node reboot: healthy baseline captured, restart acknowledged (connection drop, boot_id change, uptime 0), and post-reboot recovery confirmed with the encrypted volume auto-unlocked, auto-mounted at /srv/secure, and test data intact. This also satisfies the provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol for the single managed node (node1), corroborated by the fixed before-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots. No unnecessary or unsafe mutations were found.
limitations: Only a single reboot cycle was captured; long-term reliability across multiple reboots or power-loss scenarios was not tested.

The keyfile is stored in plaintext on the same root filesystem as the encrypted image, which is a common but security-relevant design tradeoff for unattended auto-unlock; this was not flagged as a requirement violation since the task only asked for auto-unlock at boot.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands (keyfile creation, backing file creation, luksFormat, luksOpen/mkfs, crypttab/fstab edits, mount, unmount/luksClose for validation, reboot) map directly to the task or to bounded pre-reboot verification of the generated systemd units. No unrelated experiments, no failed/abandoned services (failed-services list stayed empty before and after), and package health (dpkg) was unaffected. Listening-socket and /tmp diffs between before/after snapshots are only reboot-driven PID/tmp-dir churn (systemd-private dirs, SSH/DNS sockets re-registering), not new exposure. One minor residue: a verification test file (/srv/secure/testfile.txt) was left inside the new encrypted volume rather than removed, but this is a trivial, low-risk artifact within the volume the task itself required, not an unwanted mutation to the wider system.
